The Oxford comma (also known as the serial comma) is a punctuation mark used before coordinating conjunctions in lists when there are multiple items that might be subject to misinterpretation if not included. For example, in the sentence "I plan to invite friends, politicians, and activists," the serial comma is used after "politicians" to clarify whether "activists" refers to the political activists or other activists who may be involved in different contexts.
